name: Mirza Khizr Sultan
seoTitle: Mirza Khizr Sultan: Mughal Prince in the 1857 Uprising
seoDescription: Son of Bahadur Shah Zafar, Mirza Khizr Sultan was part of the Mughal wartime leadership in Delhi during the 1857 uprising and faced British retribution after the city fell.
role: Mughal prince associated with the Delhi phase of the 1857 uprising
contribution: Mirza Khizr Sultan, one of Bahadur Shah Zafar's sons, was part of the Mughal royal wartime circle in Delhi through the 1857 rebellion. He remained in the city during the four-month siege and was present when British forces retook Delhi in September 1857. He surrendered to British officer William Hodson alongside Mirza Mughal and Mirza Abu Bakr. On 22 September 1857, Hodson executed all three at Khooni Darwaza — the Bloody Gate — shooting them in the street. The killings, carried out after formal surrender, drew criticism in British correspondence at the time.
context: Delhi and nearby North Indian theatres during the 1857-1858 anti-colonial uprising against East India Company rule.
impact: The execution of Mirza Khizr Sultan at Khooni Darwaza alongside Mirza Mughal and Mirza Abu Bakr became a noted episode in the history of British reprisals after the fall of Delhi. Hodson's decision to shoot the surrendered princes drew contemporary comment even from within British military circles. In 1857 historiography, Mirza Khizr Sultan is remembered as part of the Mughal wartime leadership circle whose elimination ended organized royal resistance in Delhi.
